title: Breaking the Million-Electron and 1 EFLOP/s Barriers: Biomolecular-Scale Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics Using MP2 Potentials
problem: High-fidelity quantum mechanical ab initio methods deliver accuracy but cannot scale to biosystems with thousands of atoms due to computational expense of four-center integrals. Traditional WF theory methods have impractical scaling for biomolecular AIMD simulations.
motivation: Accurate quantum mechanical simulation of complex biochemical phenomena is essential for understanding biosystems, but has been computationally infeasible at biomolecular scale.
method: The approach fragments the biomolecule into smaller pieces and uses MP2 perturbation theory—a quantum method that improves basic calculations by adding computed corrections—to calculate each piece separately. To sidestep four-center integrals (the expensive quantum calculations needed for accuracy), it employs resolution-of-the-identity (RI), a mathematical trick that replaces these integrals with faster approximations in both the Hartree-Fock and MP2 calculations. It then accelerates execution using GPU processors on the Frontier supercomputer and overlaps computational phases asynchronously to keep processing units busy and avoid waiting for any single step to complete.
key_novelty: Combining molecular fragmentation with MP2 perturbation theory and resolution-of-the-identity approximation eliminates the four-center integral bottleneck, enabling quantum-accurate molecular dynamics on large biomolecules.
contributions: Enables ab initio molecular dynamics of million-electron biomolecules at quantum accuracy
Achieves 1 EFLOP/s and 59% peak performance (1006.7 PFLOP/s) on Frontier using 9,400 nodes
Eliminates four-center integrals through resolution-of-the-identity approximation for gradients
Implements asynchronous time stepping to overlap computation and reduce load imbalance
